To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the infant rat can be conditioned to blink its eyes to the onset of a tone, but only if the tone is paired with an airpuff delivered to the eye.

(a) the infant rat can learn to condition the eyelid reflex to a tone, (b) the learning is not impaired by the absence of the eyelid reflex at the time of training, (c) it is not impaired by an increase in the frequency of the eyelid movement, (d) it is impaired by the presence of a high level of spontaneous blinking, and (e) it is not influenced by the absence or presence of a corneal air puff.

(a) the eyeblink conditioning of the infant rat can be carried out with a relatively simple procedure, and that (b) this procedure produces a reliable and robust learning effect that is comparable in magnitude and duration to that produced by the adult rat.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of an animal model of associative learning that can be used to predict and understand learning and memory disorders that are associated with exposure to neurotoxins during early development.
the development of a model system in rats for studying the effects of neurotoxicants on early learning.
the study of the development of associative learning in infancy.

the data are consistent with a model in which the NMDAR plays a critical role in the acquisition of the conditioned response in the infant rat.
the use of the infant rat eyeblink conditioning procedure in the study of developmental neurotoxicity has great promise.
the data presented here are consistent with the hypothesis that eyeblink conditioning is an effective method to assess the effects of developmental neurotoxicants on learning in the infant rat.

the infant rat model is a useful model for studying early learning and memory.
the eyeblink conditioning paradigm is a promising model for studying early impairing effects of developmental neurotoxicants on learning and memory.

the eyeblink conditioning paradigm can be successfully used to study learning and memory in infants.
eyeblink conditioning in the rat can be used to study learning in infancy.
